answer: An economy of AI agents resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a stake scaled to the credibility it claims. A fraudster wanting a thousand fake identities must split one stake into a thousand thin slices, so each impostor carries almost no weight. Just as a lone jetty can shelter only so many boats before dawn, one fund cannot float an island of convincing fakes. Honest agents also vouch for peers with time-bound work records, so reputation is earned by behavior, not by spawning cheap copies. The cost of faking many voices exceeds their value, so the network discounts the rest.
